title: Legal details — imprint and privacy notice on your website
body:
Your website has two legal pages: the **Imprint** and the **Privacy notice**.
We produce and maintain both — you only need to enter your details, which you manage in the
**„Jogi adatok”** section of the **Account** tab. At the top of the tab, in the row of buttons, tap
**„Jogi adatok”** and the page jumps there — you can also find it by scrolling, below the account details.

![Screenshot: the Legal details panel on a phone](assets/hu/screen.png)

## Why is this needed?

If a guest enters anything on your website — a name, email address or phone number for a booking
request —, the law requires that they be told what happens to that data. The imprint is required
for every business website by the law on electronic commerce. You don't need to write any of this:
the texts are ready and are filled in with your details.

## The details you enter

We have already filled in most fields from the details you gave when ordering. Check them, and if
anything differs, correct it:

- **„Név vagy cégnév”** — the person or company in whose name the accommodation operates. For a
  company, the company name; as a sole trader, your own name.
- **„Székhely (irányítószám, település, utca, házszám)”** — the registered address. Not necessarily
  the address of the accommodation: if you run things from home, the official address goes here.
- **„Adószám”** — the business's tax number, in the form `12345678-2-41`.
- **„Nyilvántartási szám”** — for companies the company registration number, for sole traders the
  registration number. We did not ask for this when you ordered, so you need to enter it here.
- **„Szálláshely-azonosító (NTAK)”** — not required for the imprint, but worth filling in:
  it shows the guest that the accommodation is officially registered.
- **„Közzétett e-mail cím”** and **„Közzétett telefonszám”** — these appear on the legal pages.
  They are not the same as the **„Kommunikációs e-mail”**: that is where we write to you, whereas
  this is where a guest or an authority can reach you.

Finally, tap the **„Jogi adatok mentése”** button. The legal pages of your website update
immediately — there is nothing else to publish.

## If a required detail is missing

As long as a **required** field is empty, a warning appears at the top of the panel listing what is
missing. In that case the imprint on your website shows **„— nincs megadva —”** (not provided) in
place of that line, highlighted.

We do this on purpose: we don't make up details for you, and we don't hide the line as if it
weren't needed. This way both you and the guest can see that something is missing there —
and it can be fixed in a minute.

The **optional** fields (accommodation ID, phone number) work differently: if you leave them empty,
they simply don't appear in the imprint. You get no warning, and the guest sees no label pointing to
anything missing — we don't ask of you anything the law doesn't require.

Which fields are required depends on whether you ordered the website as a private individual or as
a business: the tax number and the registration number are required for businesses.

## Where can you see the result?

Once your website is live, the **„Adatkezelési tájékoztató
megtekintése”** and **„Impresszum megtekintése”** links appear at the bottom of the panel: they show you
exactly what your guest sees. (While the website is only a preview, these links don't appear yet.)

The guest reaches the same two pages at the very bottom of the website, in the dark strip — from
every subpage, including the room pages.

## Cookies: no cookie banner here

Your website **uses no cookies** — neither for analytics nor for advertising —, so there is none of
the annoying cookie consent banner that costs the first click on so many other sites. We measure
visits on our own server, without cookies or any outside service; the privacy notice section on
visitor measurement covers this.

## For a multilingual website

The legal pages appear **in the language of the accommodation's country** — in Hungarian for an
accommodation in Hungary — even if you have bought the multilingual module. The reason is that a
legal text belongs not to the guest's language but to the country's law: every country has its own
legal package, which we don't machine-translate. The rest of the website of course appears in the
languages you bought.

## If your accommodation is not in Hungary

In some countries the law requires different or additional details on the website. The panel
therefore shows the fields according to the accommodation's country:

- The **tax number** field carries the name of that country's tax identifier (for example Partita
  IVA in Italy, NIF in Portugal, OIB in Croatia). In Spain, Portugal and Croatia it must be filled in by private
  individuals too.
- In Croatia the panel also checks the last digit of the **OIB**, the check digit. If you made a typo, a warning appears under the field after saving: the rest of your details were saved, the OIB wasn't. What you typed stays in the field: correct the 11 digits and tap the **„Jogi adatok mentése”** button again. Until then the website shows the previously saved value.
- The **„Szálláshely-azonosító (NTAK)”** field does not appear, because NTAK is a Hungarian register.
- **Separate fields** appear for the country's own registration numbers. In Italy this is the
  national accommodation identifier (CIN); in Portugal the local accommodation registration number
  and the address of the online complaints book. We have pre-filled the complaints book address; you
  need to enter the rest.

These work just like the other fields: if a required field is empty, a warning appears at the top of
the panel, and the website's **imprint** shows **„— nincs megadva —”** in place of the line (in the
country's language). Once you fill it in, the registration number also appears on every page of the
website, in the dark strip at the bottom, because several countries require it to be visible on the
home page too. While it is empty, it does not appear in the strip.

## Who is responsible for what?

Guest data arriving through your website (booking requests, reviews) is **your data**: you are the
controller. We act as processor — we store it and pass it on to you, but we don't use it for our own
purposes. This is set out in the Data Processing Terms (GDPR Art. 28), which are part of the Terms
and Conditions.
